messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Arbormedic — dedicated GPU qualification recap + asks

Hi Samuel / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I tried to keep this short and action-focused.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Real-time triage assistant is CPU/GPU sensitive: peak throughput during daytime clinician usage spikes (~11am–3pm) and nightly batch retrain jobs.
- Security: PHI scope requires VPC + customer-managed KMS and audit logs retained 2 years.
- Determinism: you want consistent p95 latency under load for triage inference (target ~120–150 ms for 512-token average).
- Cost: commercial goal to keep incremental inference cost under $0.002/token-equivalent.

Technical constraints & preference
- Prefer isolated, reserved capacity (no noisy neighbors) for triage endpoints.
- Some models will be quantized (we discussed q8_0 for most workloads) — but you may keep higher-precision variants for fallback.
- Nightly retrain / eval window needs burst capacity for up to 4–6 hours.

Our proposal (high level)
- Dedicated pool: 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs for steady throughput with 4x burstable GPUs for nightly batch (can be time-limited).
- Isolation: single-tenant pool with VPC peering and KMS integration — Redwood Private mode.
- SLOs: target 99.9% availability + p95 latency SLO 150 ms for inference routes; can-canary rollouts + fallback to smaller, cheaper model under load.

Action items (owners & timing)
1) Arbormedic: send SOC2/PII handling questionnaire + sample audit scope (Priya) — by EOD Thu 2027-09-02.
2) Redwood: shared initial capacity estimate + cost outline (Camila) — attached; follow-up detailed ops runbook draft (Lauren) — by Fri 2027-09-03.
3) Tech sync: schedule a 60m session (engineering + infra) to validate traffic profile and KV-cache warm-up approach (Samuel & Camila) — propose Tue 2027-09-07.

Attachments: initial-capacity-estimate.xlsx (high-level throughput -> GPU mapping), SLA request PDF you mentioned.

If that all looks right I’ll convert this into a short MOU we can use for procurement cadence.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes

Camila,

Thanks for the thorough recap — this mirrors our notes. A couple clarifications:
- Our primary production model will be a trimmed GPT-like encoder-decoder with avg token length ~220 at inference.
- The 150 ms p95 is an aspirational target; to be pragmatic we’d accept up to 200 ms p95 during daytime spikes if the cost delta is large.
- Nightly burst: it should be preemptible (cheaper) as long as we get guaranteed minimum throughput for 90% of the window.

We’ll get the SOC2 questionnaire back to you (Priya will own). We can meet Tue 9/7 10:00 PT for the tech sync — sounds good.

One ask on your side: can you include a proposed canary cadence (traffic split, duration) and a stub rollback policy in the ops runbook?

Best,

Subject: Arbormedic — ops runbook draft + next milestone (attached)

Hi all,

Following our internal review Ben and Lauren pulled together a short ops runbook draft (attached) and a two-page SLA note. Highlights:
- Proposed reserved pool: 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (steady) + 4 preemptible burst GPUs.
- Canary plan: 5% traffic for 30m -> 20% for 60m -> 50% for 4h; automatic rollback on error-rate > 1.5x baseline or p95 increase > 40% vs baseline.
- Fallback: route to q4_0 quantized variant for non-critical endpoints; maintain q8_0 for triage core model.
- KV cache: automated prefix caching during canary ramp; warm-up job recommended 10–15 minutes before peak window.
- Audit & compliance: KMS integration checklist + log retention config set to 2 years.

Please review the attached Arbormedic_SLA_Request_v1.pdf and runbook. Next milestone: SOC2 questionnaire back from Arbormedic + mutual sign-off on the proposed reserved numbers by Tue 2027-09-07 so ops can schedule provisioning.

If this looks good I’ll draft a short MOU and route to finance for a provisional quote.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
